messages:
jamie: Quick RFC follow-up on multiplexed private endpoint connector vs per-tenant proxy. TL;DR: multiplexing saves IPs and infra cost but complicates SNI/authn, source-IP preservation, and blast radius. looking for tradeoffs and ops/backout concerns.

andrew: I lean multiplex for the mid/small tiers. IP exhaustion is getting real and ENI quotas bite. multiplexing + tenant routing rules reduces per-customer infra. :+1:

sophia: big concern: isolation. if a single backend gets noisy we can affect many tenants. we'd need stronger per-tenant circuit breakers and tenant-level QoS. also compliance customers will push back. :thinking_face:

mike: per-tenant proxies give us neat audit boundaries and simpler logging (one stream per customer). for SOC2/PXI it’s easier. cost is the downside but ops is simpler.

ellie: TLS question — do we terminate at the regional relay (and manage certs) or SNI passthrough to customer certs in their VPC? passthrough keeps tenant certs private but limits visibility for us.

jamie: notes from the spike: we can support three modes: `passthrough` (SNI -> tenant endpoint), `terminate` (relay handles TLS + mTLS to backend), `hybrid` (SNI passthrough for enterprise, terminate+inspect for hosted tenants). main implementation gaps: routing table scale, SNI mapping cache, and NAT-preserve-src logic.

andrew: ops/backout story: multiplexed front-door must support per-tenant kill-switch (flip header rewrite -> 502) and instant route pinning to a dedicated proxy. Without that, rollback is painful.

sophia: observability: we'd need tenant-tagged traces at the front-door and per-tenant rate metrics. also alerting when a tenant's error % impacts aggregated frontend p50/p95.

jamie: performance tradeoff — multiplexing adds an extra routing hop and JS route-lookup cost but can reduce cross-tenant cold-starts by pooling connections and using shared KV-cache for prefixes. main CPU pressure will be connection multiplexor and SNI table lookup.

ellie: on source IP: if we NAT at relay to preserve backend connectivity, we lose original srcip for tenant logs. idea: spoof `x-forwarded-for` + signed token header with original ip, but some customers require true src preservation (e.g., IP allowlists). per-tenant ENI or dedicated path is only full solution.

mike: compliance ask: enterprise customers often require pinned ENIs or private peering. hybrid model gives them that but we should not expose that as default.

jamie: propose hybrid rollout plan: 1) implement multiplexed passthrough for self-serve customers (no cert management for us), 2) add per-tenant pinning path for enterprise (reserved ENI / proxy), 3) have fast-cutover playbook that re-pins a tenant from multiplexed to dedicated path.

andrew: sample routing policy we prototyped:
```
route {
  match: host:sni("tenant.example.com")
  mode: passthrough
  fallback: pin_to: "tenant-proxy-arn"
  circuit_breaker: 5xx_rate>3% -> isolate
}
```

jamie: open questions for architecture sign-off: - acceptable blast radius for multiplexed layer? - required SLAs for enterprise customers when pinned? - minimum observability signals we need before enabling multiplexed for >100 tenants?

sophia: suggested guardrails before enabling multiplexed: tenant-level quotas, per-tenant circuit breakers, tokenized trace headers, and a per-tenant kill-switch API. without those, too risky.

jamie: action items: spike for isolation patterns (simulating noisy backend) -> andrew + ellie (due EOD next Friday). ops playbook for cutover/backout -> sophia + mike (draft by mid-week). i'll flesh perf budget and SNI cache design.

deploy-bot: CI: multiplex-proxy-spike branch passed e2e smoke tests (image: rwd/multiplex-spike:canary). :tada:

jamie: thanks all — will summarize these points in the RFC follow-up doc and propose a phased rollout with the guardrails above. if anyone has strong objections to hybrid as the default path for enterprise, speak now. :eyes:
